annotations.title: Costs order decoder (PD 44 para 4.2 and the deemed orders)

description: Explains what a costs order in England and Wales means, from the words of the order or the wording picked from a list: costs in any event, costs in the case or in the application, costs reserved, claimant's or defendant's costs in the case, costs thrown away, of and caused by, here and below, no order as to costs, summary and detailed assessment, payment on account, indemnity or standard basis, an order silent on costs, deemed orders (Part 36 acceptance, discontinuance, strike-out for an unpaid fee), wasted costs and non-party costs. Says who recovers the costs under each way the case can end, whether anything is payable now and how the amount is decided, with the rule, and how family proceedings and employment tribunals differ. It explains: it never puts a figure on costs.

date.description: The date the order was made, for the date a stated sum is due (YYYY-MM-DD).

forum.description: The kind of proceedings (default civil): "civil" (Civil (CPR)), "family" (Family (FPR)), "tribunal" (Employment tribunal).

party.description: Who has the benefit of the order, to make the answer specific. Leave out to use the party the order names.

pick.description: Instead of text, the wording: "costs" (costs, or costs in any event), "in-the-case", "in-the-application", "reserved", "own-in-the-case" (claimant's or defendant's costs in the case), "thrown-away", "of-and-caused-by", "here-and-below", "no-order", "summary" (a sum stated in the order), "detailed" (to be assessed if not agreed), "immediate" (assessed immediately or forthwith), "on-account", "proportion" (a share of the costs), "indemnity", "standard", "silent" (the order says nothing about costs), "part36" (Part 36 offer accepted), "discontinuance", "fees-strike-out" (struck out for an unpaid fee), "wasted", "non-party", "preparation-time" (employment tribunal), "follow-the-event".

special.description: Special cases that apply: "qocs" (A personal injury claim (QOCS)), "legalAidReceiving" (The party receiving costs is legally aided), "legalAidPaying" (The party paying costs is legally aided), "child" (A child or protected party is involved), "lip" (A litigant in person receives the costs), "frc" (A fixed recoverable costs claim), "smallClaims" (The small claims track).

text.description: The words of the order about costs, e.g. 'Costs of the application reserved. Otherwise, costs in the case.' Names and sums can be left out.
